A grant from the state Department of Transportation is expected to help alleviate backups and delays at traffic signals along Route 309 in Wright Twp. Township officials this week were notified the municipality has been awarded a $159,144 Pennsylvania 2026 Green Light-go grant for its traffic signal enhancement project. “We are excited that we are going to modernize the traffic lights and hope this solves the timing issues,” said pamela Heard, township manager. She noted that the project will involve modernization of the timing technology for traffic signals at Crestwood Drive, William Sword Drive and Church Road. It also will include installation of small backup generators so that the traffic signal lights will stay on in the event of a power interruption. Rice Twp. news The Rice Twp. police department is sponsoring a back-to-school supply drive to help make sure local students have the tools they need for a successful school year. Through Aug. 20 the department is collecting new school supplies including pencils, crayons, notebooks, pocket folders, pencil cases, children’s scissors, glue sticks, rulers, erasers, pencil sharpeners and backpacks. Donations can be dropped off at the Rice Twp. municipal building, 3000 Church Road. Earlier this year Rice Twp. applied for $70,000 state grant earmarked for the Nuangola Drive project. With the state’s budget in place, township officials said they expect the funds to be released, allowing the project to move forward. The township has applied for a $1 million state Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED) multimodal grant to resurface roads in Woodland Estates, Polonia Estates and Woodberry Manor. The work was recommended by PennDOT Local Technical Assistance Project (LTAP) consultant. The township also plans to investigate solutions for the flooding of Aleksander Boulevard and rework Weyhenmeyer Road drainage. Contract awarded Wright Twp. supervisors at a special meeting last week awarded a $308,704 contract to HRI, Inc. for the Stone Hedge paving project. The project will be funded through a $150,000 Local Share Account (LSA) grant and Liquid Fuel money. Earlier this summer the company was awarded a $849,290 contract for paving Walden Drive from Route 309 to an area near Red Coat Road. The work also includes the reconstruction of the entrance to Walden Park. Family Night in the Park Wright Twp. Family Night in the Park will be held Friday, Aug. 14 at the township park with the movie “Minecraft” set to begin at dusk. The movie is free and open to the public. Bring a chair or blanket to sit on to watch the movie Lonestar Sno Cone truck will be on hand to sell snow cones. Hose company receives funding Mountain Top Hose Co. No. 1 recently received $4,500 from the Congressman Rob Bresnahan and his wife, Chelsea’s Green Light Project which is administered by The Luzerne Foundation. The money will be used for a new furnace for the apparatus bay to keep equipment in a climate-controlled environment prolonging its lifespan and keeping it ready in all weather. The hose company auxiliary will hold a potato pancake pop up on Friday, August 28. Cost is $2 each or three for $5. Pre-orders are required for orders of two dozen or more to keep the lines moving. Contact Jina at (570) 328-6623 to place a large order. https://www.politico.eu/article/british-.text: LONDON — Andy Burnham has deepened Britain’s support for Ukraine by boosting the war-torn country’s ability to develop long-range missiles, in his first major move on foreign policy since becoming prime minister. To mark the PM’s visit to Ukraine — his first overseas trip since taking office last month —Downing Street announced that the U.K. government will allow European defense company MBDA to declassify information about British-made components of the Anglo-French Storm Shadow/SCALP missiles in order to help Ukraine build its own version. The missile initiative puts pressure on German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who had called for German-Swedish Taurus cruise missiles to be given to Ukraine while he was in opposition, only to backtrack after taking office — and who opted out of attending independence day festivities in Kyiv on Monday. Advertisement Advertisement The trip gave Burnham his first chance to show his commitment to the Coalition of the Willing — a grouping of Ukraine’s allies championed by his predecessor, Keir Starmer — as he co-chaired its latest meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron. Burnham was allowed to enjoy the limelight as the only E3 leader to attend the session in person, with Macron hosting Saudi Arabia’s Mohammed bin Salman and Merz attending to a domestic crisis. Sitting alongside Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Burnham said Russian threats against the U.K. will not deter him and show British assistance is having an impact. The British PM said: “It’s clear Russia is running out of options so Putin is now hoping he can win through a campaign of terror using ballistic missiles against Ukrainian civilians.” The new agreement on missiles is unlikely to have any short-term impact on Russia’s war against Ukraine, but represents a gradual shift in the U.K.’s posture towards deeper cooperation with Kyiv and sharper confrontation with Moscow. Burnham has also signed a deal allowing the U.K. to access Ukraine’s Avengers AI lab, allowing both sides to collaborate on the development of new battlefield technology, using sensors and cameras to capture and collate information on objects such as tanks, artillery, air defense systems and drone targets. Advertisement Advertisement Speaking in front of St. Sofia Cathedral in Kyiv to mark the 35th anniversary of the nation’s independence, Burnham said: “This is the moment to keep up the pressure on Russia, the moment to squeeze their ability to fund this illegal war.” He vowed that “despite Russia’s outrageous threats to my country we will continue our support for Ukraine.” Turning up the temperature Germany’s Merz is facing fresh criticism of his stance from within his own parliamentary group, from his coalition partner, and from the opposition. “It’s a clear sign that both countries are no longer waiting for Germany or relying on Germany in this matter,” CDU/CSU foreign policy politician Roderich Kiesewetter told POLITICO. He added that the British-French initiative was “a call to Germany that, unfortunately, will once again have no effect and also highlights our limited credibility.” Merz most recently justified his refusal to supply Taurus missiles during a government question session in the Bundestag in March, stating that his support for the idea, expressed while he was in the opposition, had been made “in a different context” — specifically, when Germany had more Taurus missiles for its own defense. Yet the move comes at a particularly fraught moment for British relations with Russia, after The Times reports that Moscow has withdrawn its ambassador in London without appointing a replacement. Advertisement Advertisement Asked about the decision on British missile technology, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov accused Britain of “methodically and regularly adding fuel to the fire and methodically and regularly plotting to prevent any progress in the peace process.” Al Carns, a Labour MP who resigned as U.K. armed forces minister earlier this summer over defense funding, told POLITICO the announcement is “a welcome step forward” but should not be seen as an “escalation.” He suggested it is the equivalent of Iran sharing drone technology with Russia. John Foreman, a former U.K. defense attaché to Russia and Ukraine, said it was “an evolution of position worked out over many months” and “will give Ukraine another string to its bow” at a time when the U.S. is not providing assistance with long-range missiles. He added: “It shows we won’t be bullied by Russian threats and bluster nor deterred from supporting Ukraine now and in the future.” A Ukrainian official, granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, hailed Burnham’s show of solidarity as “very significant,” backed up by “a great deliverable.” The prime minister’s spokesman declined to say the U.K. is adopting a tougher posture, telling journalists: “Our position in support of Ukraine has always been clear. We have invested billions of pounds into helping them win the fight against Russia. We’ve cracked down on Russia in terms of economic sanctions, and that this is a continuation of that stance.” Advertisement Advertisement Words or actions? The U.K.’s latest announcement has been in train for several months, according to two people with knowledge of the process, and will run alongside Operation Brakestop — the U.K.’s project with Ukraine to develop low-cost long-range strike weapons. U.K. officials played down any heightened risk of retaliation with Russia, with one senior Whitehall figure, also granted anonymity to speak freely, saying that Moscow’s words did not appear to be matched by any tangible change in their actions. Matthew Savill, director of military sciences at RUSI, said: “The Russians would almost certainly want to try and locate and destroy any such factory [producing advanced missiles,] but this is hardly an escalation given that SCALP and Storm Shadow were launched at targets inside Russia two years ago, and other Western companies are already assisting with repair and production inside Ukraine.” This article has been updated. Dan Bloom and Hans von der Burchard contributed reporting.

https://www.mediafax.ro/english/grindean.text: Grindeanu: The pay law is “sublime”; the problem is that it “is completely absent” “The pay law is sublime—some say—but the problem is that it’s completely missing!” said Sorin Grindeanu. The PSD leader argues that the draft has not been presented to employees, unions, or political parties, and asserts that, under these circumstances, there can be no political agreement on it. “There are still a few hours until the meeting at Cotroceni and 10 days until the PNRR deadline, and no one has seen a draft. We have a law for employees, without the employees knowing anything about it. Without the unions knowing anything. Without the political parties knowing what calculations are being prepared for the revenues of key systems. “There’s no way there can be a political agreement on a law that no one has seen,” Grindeanu stated on Facebook. The PSD president says the party will participate in the consultations at Cotroceni, but notes that the party is surprised by reports of “offers too good to refuse” for employees, given that the pay scales have not been made public. “The PSD will be present at the meeting at Cotroceni out of respect for Romanians and for the Presidential Administration, under whose auspices these discussions were convened,” he stated. Grindeanu also criticizes the way in which the PNL and USR allegedly negotiated with the European Commission regarding the commitments in the PNRR. According to the PSD leader, the Minister of Investments and European Projects, Dragoș Pîslaru, did not travel to Brussels for negotiations with European Commission representatives but instead submitted a draft law, for which he subsequently faced criticism. In contrast, Grindeanu maintains that the PSD has successfully renegotiated certain provisions of the PNRR in the past, citing the 9.4% threshold for pensions, funding allocations for highways, and the extension of the operational life of certain energy facilities. “The PSD does not have a draft wage law. We will only support a clear law, based on fairness, in which employees do not lose any of their current income!” concluded Sorin Grindeanu. "A lot about the AfD reminds me today about the path the Nazis took to power," the 93-year-old Knobloch told the daily Augsburger Allegemeine . She said the party "teems with Jew-haters and extremists" — something she said had already existed before, "but once, such parties disappeared from the scene very fast." This would not be the case with the AfD, she said: "It has broad support in the population, not least with young people." The party spouts hatred, including "hatred of Jews," she said. "Unfortunately, no one has managed to clamp down on it so far, so it needs to be banned," she said, even if this is "perhaps difficult legally." Knobloch called on voters in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania on Sunday to "read the newspaper, listen to the radio and watch TV; then you can't help seeing that the AfD is a profoundly anti-democratic party." She also warned that Jews in Germany were "literally under fire once more," with much reminding here of the 1920s and early 1930s. "There is hatred of Jews from right, from left and from the Muslim milieu," she said. "The threat situation for German seaports has intensified considerably," Florian Keisinger, the managing director of the Association of German Seaport Operators (ZDS), told the Welt newspaper. Keisinger said that as major hubs, ports were likely targets for cyberattacks, espionage and sabotage . Norman Zurke, the managing director of the UVHH, an association representing the interests of employers at the port of Hamburg , told the paper that he felt cyberattacks were the main danger. "However, the entire logistics sector is also already affected by sabotage," he said. He said that protecting critical infrastructure was a state responsibility and called for more investment by the federal government in protective measures for the port. Read this DW preview for everything you need to know about Oktoberfest 2026 . https://p.dw.com/p/5Mstn Skip next section Campaigns wrap up ahead of Sunday elections 09/19/2026 September 19, 2026 Campaigns wrap up ahead of Sunday elections Parties vying for power in Sunday's elections in two German states are wrapping up their campaigns with several events. In the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and the leftist environmentalist Green Party are both holding large rallies. In Berlin, the center-right Christian Democrats (CDU) of Chancellor Friedrich Merz and the left-wing populist Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) will also be staging big events. Other parties concluded their campaigns on Friday. Many voters undecided This comes as a large proportion of voters in both states seem unsure about who they will cast their ballot for. According to the "Politbarometer Extra" survey by public-service broadcaster ZDF, 21% of voters in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and 23% in Berlin remained undecided as of Thursday evening. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a tight contest is expected between the AfD and the center-left Social Democrats (SPD) , while the Greens are polling around the 5% needed to enter the state parliament at all. The state is currently governed by a SPD-Left coalition under Premier Manuela Schwesig of the SPD. In Berlin, surveys show the CDU in a neck-and-neck race with The Left party, while the BSW could fall below the 5% parliamentary threshold. Berlin's government currently consists of a coalition between the CDU and the SPD under CDU Mayor Kai Wegner. Merz's future at stake Results from the elections could have repercussions at federal level, with Merz's political future under debate after his CDU's drubbing at the hands of the AfD in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt two weeks ago. Surveys in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have shown the CDU polling at just 6%.
